title: The Succubus Club
summary: Chicago's long-lived nightclub and a favourite hunting ground of the Kindred.

claims.text: The club fills an old brick warehouse on State Street in Chicago and has stayed popular since it opened in 1982, an unusually long run for a nightclub.
Its crowds of mortal patrons draw the Kindred.
Brennon Thornhill opened it on May 23, 1982, in the former Stardust disco, amid controversy over the deaths of several basement construction workers.
A Colombian owner rumoured to have underworld ties paid for the refit.

title: Reality, Elysium and the Labyrinth
summary: The three main floors of the Succubus Club.

claims.text: The main dance floor is nicknamed Reality, the balcony above it is called Elysium as a joke among Kindred, and the basement concert hall is the Labyrinth, which really holds a maze.
The Labyrinth has its own back entrance with a neon sign; Elysium is marked by signs, but Reality is only a nickname.
Elysium runs around the walls 15 feet above the floor, is quieter, and draws the older patrons.
Anarchs seldom attend the VIP lounge parties and claim to scorn them, but many secretly envy those invited.

title: Brennon Thornhill
summary: Owner and host of the Succubus Club.

claims.text: Brennon Thornhill keeps several havens around Chicago and seldom spends the day at the club, though the third-floor suite is lavish.
Bribes and political friends helped bury an old DEA probe of the club.
Penthouse parties at the club have become places where candidates meet celebrities to win donations and endorsements.
Thornhill runs a quiet whispering campaign against the rival club the Blue Velvet, fearing the Kindred clientele will move there.
